question: What share of reported major injuries at work are caused by slips and trips?
reference_answer: On average slips and trips cause 40 per cent of all reported major injuries; they are the most common cause of injury at work.

question: What are the lower and upper exposure action values for daily noise exposure at work?
reference_answer: Lower exposure action value 80 dB and upper exposure action value 85 dB (daily or weekly personal exposure); peak sound pressure 135 and 137 dB(C).

question: When does a construction project have to be notified to HSE under CDM 2015?
reference_answer: When construction work is scheduled to last longer than 30 working days and have more than 20 workers working simultaneously at any point, or to exceed 500 person days.

question: What are HSE's five steps for managing contractors safely?
reference_answer: Step 1 planning, step 2 choosing a contractor, step 3 contractors working on site, step 4 keeping a check, step 5 reviewing the work.

question: Which areas of work do HSE's stress Management Standards cover?
reference_answer: Six areas: demands, control, support, relationships, role and change.

question: Which management model did HSE move away from when it adopted Plan, Do, Check, Act?
reference_answer: POPMAR — Policy, Organising, Planning, Measuring performance, Auditing and Review.

question: What is the minimum first-aid provision every workplace must have?
reference_answer: A suitably stocked first-aid kit, an appointed person to take charge of first-aid arrangements, and information for employees about first-aid arrangements.

question: If a display screen user needs glasses just for screen work, does the employer have to pay?
reference_answer: Yes. If a user requests an eye test the employer must provide one, and if glasses are needed specifically for DSE work the employer must pay for a basic pair of frames and lenses.

question: How far should window openings be restricted in health and social care premises to prevent falls?
reference_answer: Window restrictors should restrict the opening to 100 mm or less and be robust enough to withstand foreseeable force.

question: How often does LOLER require hoists used for lifting patients to be thoroughly examined?
reference_answer: Thorough examination by a competent person at six-monthly intervals, or in accordance with a written scheme of examination.

question: Should people riding quad bikes (ATVs) on farms wear helmets, and which kinds are suitable?
reference_answer: Yes, always wear a helmet — many ATV deaths were head injuries. Suitable types include motorcycle, equestrian, specialist ATV, cycle and mountaineering helmets.

question: Can children ride on tractors on a farm?
reference_answer: No child under 13 may drive or ride on tractors and other self-propelled agricultural machines (PACAR 1998); it is also illegal to carry children under 13 in the cab.

question: What is the workplace exposure limit for respirable crystalline silica?
reference_answer: 0.1 mg/m3 of respirable dust, averaged over 8 hours.

question: What toilet and washing facilities need to be provided on a construction site?
reference_answer: Adequate toilets and washing facilities from the start; so far as reasonably practicable flushing toilets and running water connected to mains water and drainage, otherwise units with built-in water supply and drainage tanks. A cold tap and chemical toilet alone are not adequate.

question: How many workers in Great Britain suffered from work-related ill health in 2024/25?
reference_answer: 1.9 million workers (new or long-standing) in 2024/25.

question: What was the estimated number of workers with work-related ill health in 2023/24?
reference_answer: 1.7 million workers in 2023/24.

question: How many construction workers were killed at work in 2024/25?
reference_answer: 35 fatal injuries to workers in 2024/25 (provisional), compared with an annual average of 40 over 2020/21–2024/25.

question: How many fatal injuries to workers were there in agriculture, forestry and fishing in 2024/25?
reference_answer: 23 fatal injuries to workers in 2024/25 (provisional), against a five-year annual average of 25.

question: How many manufacturing workers suffer from work-related ill health?
reference_answer: 101,000 workers (new or long-standing), averaged over 2022/23–2024/25.

question: What three areas does HSE's workplace transport guidance organise risk controls around?
reference_answer: Safe site (design and activity), safe vehicle and safe driver.

question: What health risks do isocyanate paints pose to SMART repair sprayers?
reference_answer: Occupational asthma and dermatitis.

question: Who should carry out face-fit testing of respiratory protective equipment?
reference_answer: A competent person; competence can be demonstrated through accreditation under the Fit2Fit RPE Fit Test Providers Accreditation Scheme.

question: What does a homeowner have to do under CDM 2015 when having building work done?
reference_answer: A domestic client's only responsibility is to appoint a principal designer and a principal contractor when there is more than one contractor; otherwise duties pass to the contractor/designer.

question: What are the key duties under the Confined Spaces Regulations?
reference_answer: Avoid entry to confined spaces where possible; if entry is unavoidable follow a safe system of work; and put adequate emergency arrangements in place before work starts.

question: How should I check that a contractor is competent before hiring them?
reference_answer: Make enquiries about whether they have the right combination of skills, experience and knowledge; the depth of enquiries should reflect the level of risk and complexity of the job.

question: What should a permit-to-work contain?
reference_answer: Essential elements include permit title, permit number (with references to related permits/isolation certificates), job location, plant identification, description of work, hazards and precautions, and sign-off/hand-back sections.

question: What steps must an employer work through before anyone works at height?
reference_answer: Avoid work at height where reasonably practicable; where it can't be avoided, prevent falls using a safe existing place of work or suitable equipment; minimise the distance and consequences of a fall where the risk can't be eliminated.

question: Do assaults on care workers have to be reported under RIDDOR?
reference_answer: Acts of non-consensual physical violence to a person at work that result in death, a specified injury or incapacitation for over seven days are reportable.

question: Does a small business with fewer than five employees have to write down its COSHH risk assessment?
reference_answer: Recording is required with five or more employees; with fewer than five it is not required but it makes sense to write down the steps taken and the control actions.

question: What should employers provide to support people who work alone?
reference_answer: Training, supervision, monitoring and support for lone workers.
